module_title: Bharat Ratna and Padma Awards - Posthumous Rules, Exceptions, and Records
introduction: This level explores specific exceptions, posthumous records, and unique milestones in the history of the civilian awards, which are frequently targeted in intermediate-level SSC and Railway exams.

core_concepts.title: Posthumous Bharat Ratna
core_concepts.description: When the Bharat Ratna was instituted in 1954, there was no provision for posthumous (after death) awards. This rule was amended in 1955. The very first individual to receive the Bharat Ratna posthumously was former Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri in 1966.

core_concepts.title: The Youngest and First Sportsperson
core_concepts.description: In 2014, legendary cricketer Sachin Tendulkar was awarded the Bharat Ratna. He became the youngest recipient (at 40 years of age) and the first person from the field of sports to receive this honor.

core_concepts.title: Suspensions in Award History
core_concepts.description: The civilian awards have not been continuous. They were suspended twice: first during Morarji Desai's Janata Party government (July 1977 to January 1980) and later due to pending constitutional litigations in the Supreme Court (August 1992 to December 1995).

core_concepts.title: Breaking the Maximum Limit Rule
core_concepts.description: While the unwritten rule limits the Bharat Ratna to 3 per year, historical exceptions exist. In 1999, it was given to 4 individuals. Most recently, in 2024, an unprecedented 5 individuals (Karpoori Thakur, L.K. Advani, Charan Singh, P.V. Narasimha Rao, and M.S. Swaminathan) received the honor.

important_entities.name: Lal Bahadur Shastri
important_entities.significance: India's second Prime Minister, famous for the slogan 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' during the 1965 Indo-Pak war.

important_entities.name: Nelson Mandela
important_entities.significance: The iconic anti-apartheid revolutionary and former President of South Africa.

important_entities.name: M.S. Subbulakshmi
important_entities.significance: A legendary Carnatic vocalist and the first musician ever to be awarded the Bharat Ratna.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: When counting 'foreign' winners, students mistakenly include Mother Teresa (1980). She was a naturalized Indian citizen at the time of the award, so she is officially classified under Indian recipients, not foreigners.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: Sachin hit the youngest century, and the youngest Ratna
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Link Sachin Tendulkar's early cricket achievements directly to his record as the youngest Bharat Ratna recipient at age 40.

exam_strategy_tips: Always memorize the specific years for landmark recipients, such as Lal Bahadur Shastri (1966) and Sachin Tendulkar (2014), as "Match the Following" questions heavily rely on these dates.
